title: Glessner's stable cupola stands taller and slimmer, as its photographs show
items: The dovecote cupola on the coach-house ridge now rises about a foot higher, its pyramid's point at 48 feet, as the 1887 and 1963 northwest photographs both put it once each is read against the gable beside it.
Its stone body is half a foot narrower, 5.5 feet square, and its eave reaches out nine inches instead of fifteen, closer to the trim cupola both photographs show.
The two tiers of pigeon holes ride up with it, where the 1963 photograph shows their landing ledges.
